verdict.rationale: Mailchimp Transactional documents its own email rejection denylist and allowlist, and its webhooks emit hard-bounce, spam, unsub and reject events, which implies some suppression handling. A community report also says Mailchimp removed list members over spam complaints. Nothing documents that unsubscribes, bounces and complaints are added to suppression automatically, or that suppression is shared across Marketing and Transactional sends. Missing for 10: documented automatic suppression of bounces, complaints and unsubscribes; cross-send-type (marketing plus transactional plus SMS) honoring; explicit CAN-SPAM/GDPR default-hygiene documentation; independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an ops user, unsubscribes, bounces, and spam complaints are suppressed automatically and honored across every send type — CAN-SPAM/GDPR hygiene by default

citations.quote: Adds an email to your email rejection allowlist. If the address is currently on your denylist, that denylist entry will be removed automatically.
Message events**: send, deferral, hard-bounce, soft-bounce, delivered, open, click, spam, unsub, reject
MailChimp removed half the users from a list I hadn't mailed recently, citing unverified sign-ups and spam complaints
